title: Resolve DNS redistribution on peering route mismatch causing private-hostname flapping
creator: Asha Kumar
description:
Summary: Several Dedicated customers reported intermittent failures resolving private hostnames after a VPC peering update. Symptoms: transient DNS resolution of private hostnames returned stale or public replies for ~30s-2m, followed by correct answers. Impact: customer-facing control planes experienced brief authentication/connection failures; high-severity customer escalations opened for two enterprise tenants.

Investigation notes:
- Occurs during peering route re-announcement or route refresh (BGP/route-table reconcile) from the cloud-provider side.
- Observed a short window where resolver selection fell back to external forwarders because the local resolver's routing table temporarily lacked the expected internal next-hop.
- KV cache / resolver affinity persisted and re-used an external upstream for subsequent queries until TTL-based cache invalidation occurred.
- Root cause hypothesis: order-of-operations during peering reconvergence caused ephemeral mismatch between VPC route table and our resolver binding; the resolver health-check/affinity logic does not detect transient next-hop drift and continues using an upstream that cannot answer private hostnames.

Mitigation taken: emergency feature-flagged hotfix deployed to Dedicated control-plane that forces immediate resolver affinity invalidation on peering-change webhook (rolled to 3 tenants first). Customer impact reduced but not fully eliminated for high query-rate services.

Planned fix:
1) Modify peering reconciliation flow to atomically update route state and emit a deterministic resolver-affinity-change event.
2) Update resolver affinity component to perform a fast private-hostname probe (synthetic query) after any peering change; if probe fails, switch to local resolver path and flush relevant cache entries.
3) Add guardrail to limit external-forwarder fallback during peering reconverge windows.
4) Add telemetry: histogram of TTLs observed on private-name answers and counter for fallback-triggered resolutions.

Testing & rollout: unit + integration tests to simulate route re-announcements and resolver path change. Canary across 10 dedicated tenants, progressive ramp to all Dedicated clusters over 48h with kill-switch.

Postmortem / follow-ups:
- Create runbook entry for peering oscillations and DNS fallout.
- Schedule long-term optimization: evaluate per-tenant resolver affinity cooldown tuning and faster KV cache invalidation strategies.
